_comment: EXAMPLE · ClickHouse destination / SCHEMA EVOLUTION — what happens when the frame no longer matches the table. A target is created from a NARROW frame (sku, name) and then appended to with a WIDER one (sku, name, price, category), twice: with evolution ALLOWED (schema_evolution="update", which has the connector ALTER the target before the load, adding the columns as Nullable) the new columns are added and the earlier rows read back NULL there; with it REFUSED ("strict") the write would fail, so write_wider_conformed CONFORMS the frame with a .select() — the real answer at a strict boundary, and what keeps this suite green (delete the select and re-run to see the refusal). Every table destination takes the same two values, "strict" (the default) and "update", which adds a column and widens a type; on ClickHouse too the default is "strict" — every sink here spells the value out all the same. Evolution only grows a table: a dropped, renamed or narrowed column is a migration, not evolution. The schema-evolution suites hold every table destination to the whole policy. v1 uses `replace` so the example is repeatable and v2 uses `append` so there is something to evolve; ordering comes from TWO supporting publishers with the narrow trigger declared `detached: false` as a GATE. One function per file under functions/clickhouse_dest_evolution/. Run: `tdd xp one-shot --suite examples/clickhouse_dest_evolution --keep`.
